topic: Avianca Flight 203: the bomb Pablo Escobar ordered for a presidential candidate who was not on board

sentences.text: In 1989, a bomb destroys a plane over Colombia.
Five minutes later, a bomb explodes.
The plane breaks apart over Soacha.
All 107 on board die, and three people on the ground.

sentences.editorial: turn to context, not a factual claim

sentences.text: But Gaviria is not on the plane.
He goes on to win the presidency.
Nine days later, another bomb kills sixty-three in Bogotá.
Two Americans died, so Washington starts hunting Escobar.
His chief assassin gets ten life sentences.
A 2016 report disputes the cause, but families reject it.
A bomb meant for one man killed 110.

claims.claim: Avianca Flight 203, a Boeing 727, was destroyed by a bomb over the municipality of Soacha on 27 November 1989.
claims.excerpt: It was destroyed by a bomb over the municipality of Soacha on November 27, 1989.

claims.claim: The domestic flight from Bogotá to Cali took off as scheduled at 07:13.
claims.excerpt: Flight 203 took off as scheduled at 07:13.

claims.claim: Five minutes into the flight an explosive charge detonated.
claims.excerpt: Five minutes into the flight, at a speed of 794 kilometres per hour (429 knots) and an altitude of 13,000 feet (4,000 metres), an explosive charge detonated

claims.claim: A second blast ripped the airliner apart and the wreckage was scattered in a five-kilometre radius around the town of Soacha.
claims.excerpt: A second blast ripped the airliner apart

claims.claim: All 107 people on board were killed, as well as three people on the ground.
claims.excerpt: All 107 people on board were killed, as well as three people on the ground.

claims.claim: An investigation determined that plastic explosives were used to destroy the plane.
claims.excerpt: An investigation determined that plastic explosives were used to destroy the plane.

claims.claim: The bombing had been ordered by the Medellín drug cartel; Pablo Escobar planned it in the lead-up to the 1990 elections.
claims.excerpt: Drug king Pablo Escobar, of the Medellín drug cartel, planned the bombing in the lead-up to the 1990 elections

claims.claim: Escobar hoped the bomb plot would kill presidential candidate César Gaviria.
claims.excerpt: hoping the bomb plot would kill presidential candidate C

claims.claim: Gaviria was not on the aircraft, despite Escobar's expectations, and went on to be elected president.
claims.excerpt: Gaviria was not on the aircraft, despite Escobar's expectations, and went on to be elected president.

claims.claim: Nine days after the plane bombing, the DAS Building bombing, presumably also ordered by the Medellín Cartel, killed 63 people in Bogotá.

claims.context: The article says 'presumably' about who ordered it.

claims.claim: Two Americans were among the dead, prompting the Bush administration to begin Intelligence Support Activity operations to find Escobar.
claims.excerpt: Two Americans were among the dead, prompting the Bush administration to begin Intelligence Support Activity operations to find Escobar.

claims.claim: The Medellín Cartel's chief assassin, alias 'La Quica', was convicted in a US court in 1994 and sentenced to 10 consecutive life sentences.
claims.excerpt: was sentenced to 10 consecutive life sentences

claims.claim: A 2016 El Espectador report argues the explosion was caused by a malfunctioning fuel pump; it was heavily criticized by Avianca and the victims' family members.
claims.excerpt: heavily criticized by Avianca and family members of the victims
claims.context: A disputed minority account; the bombing finding is the investigation's.
